articles.title: EUA assumem pela 1ª vez possuir armas em órbita: veja o que se sabe | G1
articles.standfirst: Armas podem ser usadas para atacar satélites inimigos. EUA também desenvolvem interceptadores espaciais para o sistema 'Golden Dome'.
articles.summary: Armas podem ser usadas para atacar satélites inimigos. EUA também desenvolvem interceptadores espaciais para o sistema 'Golden Dome'.
articles.body:
Os Estados Unidos reconheceram pela primeira vez publicamente nesta segunda-feira (14) que possuem armas de controle espacial posicionadas em órbita . A informação foi divulgada pelo secretário da Força Aérea dos EUA, Troy Meink, durante uma conferência militar.

Meink não informou quais são os equipamentos, quantas armas estão em órbita ou como elas funcionam.

“Os Estados Unidos agora têm, em órbita, armas de controle espacial capazes de defender as forças conjuntas contra adversários hostis”, disse ele durante discurso.

Segundo um funcionário do governo ouvido pelo jornal americano "The Washington Post" sob condição de anonimato, o sistema teria capacidade de destruir ou neutralizar um satélite inimigo caso ele esteja sendo usado para atingir tropas ou satélites americanos.

A Força Espacial dos EUA afirmou, em comunicado, que as capacidades de controle espacial podem ser usadas tanto para ações ofensivas quanto defensivas.

Segundo a nota, os sistemas permitem aos militares americanos disputar e controlar o domínio espacial por meios "cinéticos e não cinéticos" para afetar recursos de adversários.

A revelação representa uma mudança no discurso público dos Estados Unidos sobre a capacidade militar americana no espaço. Autoridades das Forças Armadas costumam ser cautelosas quando questionadas sobre o assunto e citam questões de segurança nacional.

Em 2022, John Raymond, primeiro chefe de operações espaciais da Força Espacial dos EUA, afirmou que o principal objetivo do país "é impedir a guerra".

Um eclipse solar total passa sobre o México, os Estados Unidos e o Canadá. Milhões de pessoas testemunharam o céu escurecer quando a Lua passou entre a Terra e o Sol. Astronautas a bordo da estação capturaram a sombra lunar atravessando o continente norte-americano. — Foto: Nasa

Os Estados Unidos não divulgaram detalhes sobre os equipamentos mencionados por Meink. A descrição oficial, porém, indica que eles podem ser empregados para interferir ou atacar sistemas espaciais de adversários.

Uma das possibilidades seria o uso contra satélites considerados uma ameaça a forças americanas. Esses equipamentos são essenciais para atividades militares como comunicação, vigilância e navegação.

A capacidade também é apresentada pelos EUA como uma forma de dissuasão, ou seja, de tentar impedir que um adversário ataque os norte-americanos ao saber que poderá sofrer uma reação.

Os Estados Unidos também estão desenvolvendo uma rede de interceptadores baseada no espaço que deverá integrar, no futuro, o sistema de defesa antimísseis Golden Dome, uma das principais iniciativas militares do governo de Donald Trump.

Meink afirmou que esses interceptadores estão agora "prontos para o voo". Não há indicação, porém, de que o armamento revelado nesta segunda-feira faça parte desse programa.

A confirmação ocorre em meio ao aumento das tensões estratégicas entre os Estados Unidos, a China e a Rússia.

Durante anos, os EUA acusaram os adversários de desenvolver e realizar manobras militares no espaço. Entre as capacidades apontadas pelos americanos estão sistemas capazes de interferir em satélites e outras tecnologias de combate espacial.

A Força Espacial dos EUA afirma que a China desenvolve capacidades espaciais e antiespaciais como parte de sua modernização militar. Já a Rússia considera o espaço um domínio de combate e também desenvolve sistemas capazes de afetar satélites.

O lançamento soviético do Sputnik em 1957 — o primeiro satélite do mundo — foi um alerta para os EUA — Foto: Universal History Archive/Universal Images Group via Getty Images

A disputa militar no espaço começou ainda durante a Guerra Fria. Pouco depois de a União Soviética lançar o Sputnik, em 1957, Estados Unidos e Moscou passaram a estudar maneiras de colocar armas em órbita e de destruir satélites.

Uma das principais preocupações na época era a possibilidade de instalação de armas nucleares no espaço.

Em 1967, Estados Unidos, União Soviética e outros países assinaram o Tratado do Espaço Exterior, que proíbe a instalação de armas de destruição em massa em órbita.

O tratado não impede, porém, o desenvolvimento de outras armas ou sistemas capazes de atingir satélites. Desde então, Estados Unidos, Rússia, China e Índia desenvolveram diferentes capacidades antissatélite.

Esses sistemas podem ser usados para atingir equipamentos fundamentais para operações militares, como satélites de comunicação, vigilância e navegação.

articles.title: Brigou no avião? Você pode ficar até um ano proibido de voar; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida entrou em vigor nesta segunda-feira (14) e também prevê multas de R$ 17,5 mil para casos de conflitos menos graves durante o voo ou o embarque.
articles.summary: Medida entrou em vigor nesta segunda-feira (14) e também prevê multas de R$ 17,5 mil para casos de conflitos menos graves durante o voo ou o embarque.
articles.body:
Enquanto confusões dentro de aviões se multiplicam em vídeos compartilhados nas redes sociais, a Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) implementa nesta segunda-feira (14) um sistema de punições a passageiros indisciplinados, que vai desde multas até a proibição de viajar em voos nacionais de qualquer companhia aérea.

A prática, conhecida em inglês como no-fly list , ou lista de proibição de voo, já é adotada em alguns países do exterior — nos Estados Unidos, por exemplo, está em vigor desde 2001, após os ataques às Torres Gêmeas, em Nova York.

Em entrevista à BBC News Brasil, o superintendente da Anac afirma que a medida atende a pedidos dos próprios passageiros e das empresas, diante do aumento dos conflitos no ar.

Segundo a Associação Brasileira das Empresas Aéreas (Abear) — que representa Latam, Gol e Azul —, foram registrados, em 2025, 1.764 casos de tumultos, brigas e depredações em aviões e aeroportos brasileiros, ante 1.059 em 2024, o que representa uma alta de 66,57% em um ano.

"Já tivemos de tudo, desde confusão entre passageiros até disparo acidental de arma e alarme falso de bomba na aeronave, provocado por um passageiro que queria pregar uma peça", relata Giovano Palma, superintendente da Anac.

Palma explica que, nas circunstâncias atuais, uma simples briga que obrigue a aeronave a retornar ao aeroporto de origem não apenas causa transtorno para todos os passageiros daquele voo e do seguinte, que utilizaria o mesmo avião, como também obriga a companhia aérea a reacomodar em outra viagem até mesmo quem provocou o conflito.

"Além disso, as contramedidas que você consegue adotar são poucas, porque você está dentro de um avião, no ar. O risco para a operação é muito grande, então a gente buscou focar esses casos gravíssimos quando pensamos na lista de proibição de voo", acrescenta.

As sanções administrativas da Anac foram criadas principalmente para atos de indisciplina em voos domésticos regulares e em aeroportos brasileiros — inclusive nas áreas em aeroportos destinadas a passageiros de voos internacionais. Mas as regras não se aplicam a voos internacionais.

Entenda, a seguir, como funcionará a nova resolução da Anac e o que muda para os passageiros.

Movimento nas salas de embarque do Aeroporto de Congonhas. (11/12/2025) — Foto: Paulo Pinto/Agência Brasil

Atos de indisciplina considerados graves vão gerar uma multa de R$ 17,5 mil ao passageiro. São eles:

Violência física contra funcionários de companhias aéreas ou aeroportos;

Violência física contra outro passageiro dentro do avião;

Danificar ou destruir intencionalmente bens da aeronave, quando isso afeta a operação;

Ameaçar ou intimidar um membro da tripulação, de forma que afete a segurança do voo;

Fazer falsa comunicação de bomba, explosivos ou armas dentro do avião.

2. O que pode gerar a suspensão de um passageiro

Passageiros podem ser banidos de voar por um ano — Foto: BBC

Atos de indisciplina considerados gravíssimos levarão o cliente à lista de proibição de voo. A sanção será aplicada pela companhia aérea em que ocorreu o conflito e compartilhada com as demais empresas, que serão obrigadas a barrar aquele passageiro também.

Isso impedirá o cliente de emitir passagens, fazer check-in e embarcar durante o período da suspensão, que varia de seis meses a um ano.

Se o passageiro já tiver comprado uma passagem para o período, aliás, terá direito ao reembolso integral, que inclui as tarifas aeroportuárias.

Mas o cliente não receberá qualquer ressarcimento relacionado ao voo em que ocorreu o ato de indisciplina, o que se aplica no caso de conexões ou escalas e haja o impedimento de seguir a viagem.

O que pode levar à suspensão por 6 meses:

Adulterar, danificar ou destruir um dispositivo de segurança do avião, mas sem impedir ou dificultar a operação;

Agredir fisicamente um membro da tripulação, como comissários e pilotos, mas sem impedir ou dificultar a operação;

Cometer violência ou atentado contra a dignidade sexual de tripulante ou passageiro, violando sua integridade física, psíquica ou liberdade sexual.

O que pode levar à suspensão por um ano:

Adulterar, danificar ou destruir dispositivo de segurança do avião e isso impedir ou dificultar a operação;

Agredir fisicamente um membro da tripulação e, com isso, impedir ou dificultar a operação;

Levar ou manusear explosivos ou armas dentro do avião, salvo exceções previstas em regulamentação;

Entrar ou tentar entrar na cabine de comando sem autorização;

Fazer qualquer tentativa ilegal de tomar o controle da aeronave.

3. Como serão aplicadas a multa e a suspensão

Movimento no Aeroporto Internacional de São Paulo, em Guarulhos. — Foto: Paulo Pinto/Agência Brasil

A multa será aplicada pela Anac, por meio de um processo administrativo que vai apurar a infração. A companhia aérea ou o aeroporto deverá comunicar o ocorrido à agência e fornecer as evidências necessárias para comprovar o ato de indisciplina e identificar o passageiro.

Já a inclusão na lista de proibição de voar será feita pela própria companhia aérea responsável pelo voo, em até cinco dias após a infração, em um sistema compartilhado pelas empresas.

O passageiro deverá ser comunicado da decisão, com a descrição do ocorrido e os canais para reclamação. Ele terá direito à defesa, e a companhia terá até cinco dias para responder à reclamação.

Se rever sua decisão, deverá retirar imediatamente o passageiro da lista. O cerceamento do direito de defesa ou a falta de comunicação ao passageiro poderá resultar em multa de R$ 35 mil para a empresa.

Em casos de infrações graves e gravíssimas, as companhias e os aeroportos terão de guardar por cinco anos os registros que comprovem a ocorrência e a autoria do ato.

As próprias empresas também poderão ser multadas se descumprirem as regras. Não aplicar a suspensão em um caso gravíssimo, por exemplo, poderá resultar em multa de R$ 70 mil. Já o descumprimento da obrigação de aderir ao sistema de compartilhamento de dados poderá gerar multa de R$ 70 mil por mês.

Todas essas medidas passarão por uma reavaliação após dois anos de vigência da resolução. A Anac ficará encarregada de produzir um relatório sobre a eficácia e os resultados das regras e indicar possíveis mudanças.

Avião da Latam decola no Aeroporto de Congonhas após suspensão temporária da operação — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Diretor-executivo do Procon, Luiz Orsatti diz que, "por ser uma agência federal, a Anac tem todo o poder para regulamentar o setor, porque há fundamento legal, mas essa regulamentação não pode contradizer o Código de Defesa do Consumidor".

A principal preocupação de alguns passageiros é que, por se tratar de um processo conduzido por pessoas, haja exageros por parte de funcionários dos aeroportos ou das companhias aéreas, que poderiam enquadrar os clientes de maneira indevida.

"Os fatos são objetivos, mas, no calor do caso, pode haver uma interpretação um pouco mais subjetiva", reconhece Orsatti.

Por isso, diz ele, qualquer passageiro que se sentir lesado pela aplicação de uma multa ou restrição pode, além de recorrer à própria companhia aérea e à Anac, buscar ajuda do Procon e da Justiça "para que discuta não a legalidade da punição", mas sua aplicação.

Ele acrescenta que o Procon foi procurado pela Anac durante a elaboração das regras e sugeriu que houvesse uma ressalva à proibição de voo para questões de caráter humanitário, mas não encontrou apoio das demais entidades envolvidas no processo.

A exceção se aplicaria, por exemplo, ao caso de um passageiro que precise viajar de avião para fazer um tratamento médico ou para uma transferência que exija rapidez.

Como essa ressalva não está prevista na resolução da Anac, esse passageiro agora precisaria tentar convencer as companhias a vender a passagem nos balcões de atendimento ou por telefone — o que, reconhece o diretor do Procon, deve ser difícil. A orientação, então, é procurar o plantão do Judiciário em busca de uma liminar.

5. Como ficará a proteção de dados pessoais

Aeroporto Afonso Pena Aeroporto de Curitiba Aeroporto São José dos Pinhais — Foto: Rodrigo Zanotto

A resolução da Anac não especifica como funcionará o sistema de compartilhamento de dados entre as companhias aéreas nos casos de inclusão de passageiros na lista de proibição de voo.

Questionada pela BBC News Brasil, a Anac disse que "a ferramenta em questão está sendo desenvolvida em conjunto entre companhias e a Empresa Nacional de Inteligência em Governo Digital e Tecnologia da Informação".

A resolução, porém, não traz detalhes sobre a proteção dos dados pessoais dos passageiros para garantir o cumprimento da Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados, conhecida como LGPD.

A Anac também não esclareceu quais dados dos passageiros incluídos na lista seriam compartilhados entre as companhias aéreas. À BBC, afirmou que "haverá mudanças nos contratos de transporte aéreo e, caso necessário, ajustes devido à LGPD".

O contrato de transporte aéreo é o documento que todos os passageiros aceitam ao comprar uma passagem.

articles.title: Dark web hacker claims to have stolen personal information of 40,000 Twitch streamers
articles.summary: US Streamers News: A database advertised on a dark web marketplace is drawing attention across the Twitch community after a threat actor claimed to possess personal info.
articles.body: A database advertised on a dark web marketplace is drawing attention across the Twitch community after a threat actor claimed to possess personal information linked to around 40,000 streamers. Cybersecurity researchers have reviewed a sample of the alleged records, but early findings suggest this may not be a straightforward Twitch data breach. The bigger concern is how the information could be used against creators.Twitch streamer data allegedly appears in dark web databaseThe database was reportedly put up for sale on an illicit marketplace on September 9. According to an investigation by Cybernews, the seller claimed the collection contained Twitch usernames, profile links, email addresses, follower counts, legal names and account verification details.Researchers examined 501 records supplied as proof of the seller’s claims. The sample reportedly included information such as usernames, profile URLs, email addresses and follower numbers. Some entries also contained creators’ real names.However, the findings do not currently establish that a hacker broke into Twitch and stole the information.One researcher who examined the sample said:“From what I see, this indeed looks like a data scrape, not a breach,”That distinction matters. Much of the information included in the database can already be found online. A streamer’s username, profile and follower count are generally visible to the public, while a legal name could potentially be pieced together through linked social media accounts or other public sources.Some follower numbers in the alleged database were also outdated. That could indicate the information was collected over time rather than through a recent attack on Twitch.There is, however, one detail that has raised further questions. Cybernews reportedly found email addresses that were not publicly displayed on the affected Twitch profiles. Researchers suggested this could point to misuse of Twitch’s API, although there is no confirmation that Twitch itself was compromised.Twitch streamers face potential phishing and scam risksEven if the database mainly consists of scraped information, putting thousands of records together creates a new security problem. A scammer no longer needs to search across different websites to build a profile of a creator.Cybernews warned:“The information of many creators is aggregated to one place, making it easier for a malicious actor to profile these people and possibly craft social engineering scams,”That could make phishing attempts much more convincing. A scammer could use a creator’s real name, email address and audience size to pose as a company offering a sponsorship deal. Another attack could imitate Twitch support and claim that the streamer needs to verify their account.The alleged database also comes amid another recent Twitch security concern. Researchers at Socket found that an unofficial browser extension called “Twitch Enhanced Viewer | JeetBot” had been forwarding live Twitch OAuth tokens to servers controlled by its operator. The extension reportedly had about 31,000 users.Twitch said the extension was not affiliated with the platform and revoked potentially exposed access tokens. Users who installed it were advised to remove it.There is currently no evidence linking that extension incident to the dark web database.For creators, the latest claims are another reminder to tighten account security. Two-factor authentication, unique passwords and caution around unexpected sponsorship offers can reduce the chances of falling for targeted scams.Twitch has not been confirmed as the source of the alleged 40,000-record database, and the claims remain under investigation. The situation therefore raises serious concerns, but it should not yet be described as a confirmed Twitch breach.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: A 15-year-old started collecting unwanted shoes after school; she has now gathered 1,913 pairs for people in need
articles.summary: US News: A school service project inspired by her late grandmother has grown into a remarkable mission to help people in need, with teenager Maggie Driscoll no.
articles.body: A school service project inspired by her late grandmother has grown into a remarkable mission to help people in need, with teenager Maggie Driscoll now working towards collecting 10,000 pairs of shoes. The Hingham resident and Tabor Academy freshman has already gathered 1,913 pairs of new and used footwear for Soles4Souls, an organisation that supports people worldwide. What began during her time at Derby Academy after she received the 2024 Foley Citizenship Prize has since expanded with support from residents and schools. Now, with 8,087 pairs still needed, Maggie is calling on communities, businesses and organisations to help her reach the ambitious target.How Maggie’s grandmother inspired the shoe driveMaggie’s motivation began with the story of her late grandmother, who was a teacher in Wisconsin and organised shoe drives for children in need at the end of each school year. That experience stayed with Maggie and later influenced her decision to apply for the Foley Citizenship Prize while she was at Derby Academy.The prize is awarded each year to a seventh-grade student who demonstrates kindness and respect towards others and wants to create positive change. After receiving the 2024 award, Maggie used her eighth-grade service project to educate her community about the importance of shoes and collect footwear for Soles4Souls. Maggie told the Hingham Anchor she had the “privilege of educating my community about the significance of shoes”, an effort that ultimately gathered thousands of pairs and became her ongoing passion project.How donated shoes help people in needFor Maggie, the project is about more than simply finding unwanted shoes and keeping them out of storage or rubbish bins. She explained that shoes can provide comfort and allow people to take part in everyday activities, while also giving them confidence and a way to express themselves.Soles4Souls also uses donated footwear to support people who turn the shoes into a source of income. As Maggie told the Hingham Anchor, the shoes can be placed “onto the feet of these individuals” while also being used as “a source of income for many” who start businesses selling the shoes they receive. That broader impact has helped drive her determination to expand the collection.Maggie’s shoe collection expands across the communityThe initiative has expanded well beyond a small school collection. Soles4Souls has rented a storage unit in Weymouth specifically for Maggie’s shoe collection, giving the project a larger space to handle donations from the local and Tabor communities.The collection accepts footwear for boys, girls, men and women, including cleats, heels, sneakers, dance shoes, sports shoes, dress shoes and casual footwear. According to Maggie, the Weymouth facility is unique in Massachusetts because it is the only shoe drop-off location in the state that accepts more than 15 pairs at a time, making it possible to accommodate larger community donations.Maggie aims to collect 10,000 pairs of shoesMaggie’s next target is considerably larger than the 1,913 pairs already collected. She hopes community support will help her reach 10,000 pairs in the new year. If she succeeds, Soles4Souls has said it will organise a local shoe event and donate 100 new pairs of shoes to a non-profit organisation in the community.Last year, as part of her Foley Prize project, Maggie raised more than $1,000 to provide Hingham schoolchildren with DSW gift cards so they could choose a new pair of shoes. She has also distributed flyers at local businesses and secured donation bins at Derby Academy and Tabor Academy. With 1,913 pairs already collected, Maggie still has 8,087 pairs to go to reach her 10,000-pair target. She is encouraging residents, businesses and other organisations to participate, including by hosting shoe donation bins in common areas.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Japan removed 1.5 million cubic metres of mercury-tainted sediment from Minamata Bay, but decades later the mercury remains buried beneath reclaimed land
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Japan’s most infamous mercury disaster left behind an unusual environmental legacy, instead of destroying the contamination, engineers dredged it from.
articles.body: Japan’s most infamous mercury disaster left behind an unusual environmental legacy, instead of destroying the contamination, engineers dredged it from the seabed and sealed it beneath newly reclaimed land. From 1974 to 1990, Kumamoto Prefecture dealt with about 1.5 million cubic metres of Minamata Bay sediment containing more than 25 parts per million of mercury. The project created a 58-hectare landfill at a cost of about ¥48.5 billion. Decades later, the reclaimed ground has become a public park, but the mercury itself remains buried beneath it.Minamata Bay carried the legacy of a mercury disasterMinamata disease was officially identified in 1956 after people around Minamata Bay began suffering severe neurological symptoms. The Japanese government concluded in 1968 that the disease was caused by eating fish and shellfish contaminated with methylmercury discharged by Chisso Corporation. The company's factory had used mercury as a catalyst in acetaldehyde production, with methylmercury forming as a by-product and entering the bay through wastewater.Stopping the discharge did not remove what had already accumulated. Mercury-containing sediment remained on the floor of the bay, where it could continue to affect marine life. The National Institute for Minamata Disease estimates that nearly 150 tons of mercury had accumulated in the seabed before the dredging and landfill operation began. Much of the mercury in the sludge was believed to have been present as inorganic mercury, including mercury sulfide.Japan removed sediment containing more than 25 ppm mercuryAfter the discharge of methylmercury was stopped, a major problem remained beneath Minamata Bay, large quantities of contaminated sediment still held mercury at potentially dangerous concentrations. Japan therefore set a provisional removal standard of 25 ppm total mercury and launched a huge dredging and landfill project to remove sediment exceeding that level.According to the Ministry of the Environment, Government of Japan, Kumamoto Prefecture carried out the project from 1974 to 1990, dealing with about 1.5 million cubic metres of bottom sediment containing mercury above the 25 ppm removal standard. The material was dredged from the bay and placed in a controlled landfill, creating approximately 58 hectares of reclaimed land. The total project cost was recorded at ¥48 billion, of which the responsible company, Chisso, bore ¥30.5 billion.The scale of the operation was extraordinary. Government records put the total treated sediment at roughly 1.51 million cubic metres, while the reclaimed landfill covered about 582,000 square metres. Rather than attempting to eliminate the mercury itself, Japan's strategy was to remove the contaminated material from the marine environment and isolate it on land.The contaminated sludge was sealed rather than destroyedThe Minamata cleanup was ultimately a massive containment project. Mercury is an element and cannot simply be destroyed through ordinary environmental treatment, so the immediate goal was to prevent mercury-laden sediment from remaining in contact with the bay's ecosystem.Dredging therefore transferred the contamination from the seabed into a controlled landfill. The Ministry of the Environment records that about 1.5 million cubic metres of sediment were handled through dredging and landfill between 1974 and 1990. The reclaimed area effectively became a permanent physical repository for material that had once formed part of the bay floor.The project also had to be considered alongside restrictions on fishing and seafood consumption that had continued for decades. According to the ministry, restrictions on taking fish and shellfish from Minamata Bay remained in place, with interruptions, until October 1997, when the dividing nets in the bay were completely removed.The reclaimed land later became associated with Eco Park Minamata, transforming part of the former bay into public land while leaving the contaminated sediment contained beneath it.Minamata Bay eventually reopened to fishingRemoving the sediment was only part of the recovery. Japan continued monitoring fish, shellfish, water and bottom sediment to track whether mercury contamination remained at levels capable of causing further exposure.The Ministry of the Environment notes that Japan's provisional regulatory standard for fish was 0.4 ppm for total mercury and 0.3 ppm for methylmercury. Monitoring of methylmercury concentrations in fish and shellfish around Minamata Bay continues.The restrictions on fishing were eventually lifted in 1997. In October of that year, the dividing nets that had separated the contaminated area from the rest of the bay were completely removed. This followed years of monitoring and marked a major step in restoring the bay to normal use.Yet the reopening did not mean that the historical mercury contamination had disappeared. Instead, a substantial portion of the pollution had been physically relocated from the seabed into an engineered landmass.The landfill leaves a question for the futureMinamata's cleanup illustrates the complicated nature of dealing with persistent pollutants. Japan succeeded in removing vast quantities of mercury-contaminated sediment from the marine environment and preventing it from continuing to circulate through the bay. But the mercury itself was not destroyed. It was contained, that distinction matters.The reclaimed land therefore became a lasting part of Minamata's environmental legacy. What had once been contamination spread across the bay floor was concentrated into a defined area that could be monitored and managed. The approach helped make the bay usable again, but it also meant that future generations would inherit responsibility for the site.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pak ups reward for Masood Azhar by PKR 20L ahead of FATF meet
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Taking its duplicity on combating terror to farcical levels, Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has declared a reward of PKR 70 lakh on UN-.
articles.body: Taking its duplicity on combating terror to farcical levels, Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has declared a reward of PKR 70 lakh on UN-designated terrorist Maulana Masood Azhar while calling him a "fugitive". The move comes ahead of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) meeting next month.Pakistan had initially included Azhar in its 'red book' in 2021, setting a bounty of PKR 50 lakh. With apprehensions of being placed back on the FATF's 'grey list', Pakistan has now raised the reward by an additional PKR 20 lakh after five years.The move comes despite Islamabad's long-standing falsehood that Azhar escaped to Afghanistan and was no longer in the country. Even after key family members overseeing Jaish-e-Mohammed operations were eliminated in Operation Sindoor, Pakistan has remained unwilling to acknowledge his presence on its territory or extradite him to India. The assessment of Indian agencies is that he is based in the Sindh province but is often moved to different locations by the ISI to escape an assassination bid.Azhar, who is believed to have escaped the attack on the JeM's headquarters in Markaz Subhanallah, Bahawalpur, is wanted in India in connection with several attacks, including the 2019 Pulwama bombing in which 40 CRPF personnel were killed.Azhar's profile in the 'red book', which lists Pakistan's most-wanted fugitives and terrorists, doesn't mention any details including national ID card or passport number, place of birth, sect or any identification mark. "The federal govt of Pakistan is offering a reward of Rs 70,00,000 for information directly leading to apprehension or conviction of Masood Azhar, the son of Khuda Baksh," it says.As it did in 2021, Pakistan has also maintained that the 26/11 Mumbai attack planners were not on its soil, as per the book. It has retained the profiles of 17 terrorists involved in the planning and financing of the Mumbai attacks, continued from 2021, but the photographs and details of two of the terrorists - Abdul Rehman and Muhammad Khan - have been removed this time. Khan had provided the boat used in the attack.The 'red book' in Pakistan is an official document published by law enforcement agencies to 'list and track' the country's most-wanted fugitives and high-profile terrorists.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: AI 'fearmongering' will be good for no one: China
articles.summary: China News: China criticised calls from leading US technology executives to put the brakes on AI development and impose tighter curbs on Chinese model makers.\"Fea.
articles.body: China criticised calls from leading US technology executives to put the brakes on AI development and impose tighter curbs on Chinese model makers."Fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance and serve the interests of no one," foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said in Beijing Monday. "The development of AI bears on the common well-being of all humanity," he added, in response to a question on calls to slow frontier models.The dispute over frontier technology is intensifying days before officials from the US and China are set to hold AI discussions ahead of Donald Trump's summit with Xi Jinping on Sept 24. China worries the US could invoke safety or national security to justify broader restrictions, said Sun Chenghao, a fellow at Tsinghua University's Center for International Security and Strategy in Beijing. "The boundary between AI safety and AI competition is becoming increasingly blurred," added Sun, who has discussed AI with US counterparts. "If every safety question becomes interpreted through the lens of strategic competition, meaningful dialogue will be difficult."In the summit lead-up, Communist Party officials also aired their own concerns. China's cyberspace regulator released an AI safety governance framework to address emerging risks.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Saudi military airbase hit as Houthis launch fresh attacks
articles.summary: Middle East News: Arab states in the Gulf called off a meeting with Iran planned for Monday, while Yemen's Houthis launched a new attack on Saudi after fighting that ha.
articles.body: Arab states in the Gulf called off a meeting with Iran planned for Monday, while Yemen's Houthis launched a new attack on Saudi after fighting that has extended the war in West Asia to another theatre.The Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen said they fired dozens of missiles and drones on Monday at a Saudi military airbase in Khamis Mushait, near the border, hitting aircraft hangars, radar systems, runways and ammunition depots. They described the attack as retaliation for hundreds of Saudi airstrikes on Yemen in recent days.Saudi authorities announced brief emergency alerts in three other southern cities which have previously come under Houthi fire. The Houthis launched a lightning advance last week in Yemen, culminating in the seizure of an island in the mouth of the Red Sea Friday. A separate attack that day, which Riyadh blamed on Iran-backed fighters in Iraq, knocked out Saudi Arabia's east-west pipeline, the main route for West Asian oil bypassing the blockaded Strait of Hormuz.Oil prices jumpCrude oil prices rose over 3% Monday, when the market reopened after the weekend, while the retail price of diesel in the US hit a new all-time high above $6.23 a gallon. Traders say the closure of the Saudi pipeline could cut off as much as 4% of global oil supply unless it is reopened within days.Oman had been due to host a meeting on Monday with Iran and Gulf states to discuss negotiations aimed at reopening Hormuz, the world's most important oil shipping lane, largely closed since the US and Israel attacked Iran at the end of Feb. But Oman's foreign minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi announced overnight that the meeting had been postponed "in the interests of consensus". Iran said the postponement was at the request of Saudi Arabia.Meanwhile, Iran issued a list of 77 ships it said had violated its protocols for operating in the Strait of Hormuz. Any ship on the list would face "curbs on future passages".Dilemma for TrumpThe upsurge of fighting in Yemen poses a dilemma for Washington, which is under pressure to aid its Saudi allies but anxious not to expand the costly war to a new theatre. articles.title: Jimmy Buffett helped turn Florida's manatee into a conservation symbol; the singer became involved with the campaign decades before the species' recovery
articles.summary: US News: Long before Jimmy Buffett became widely associated with island music, boats and Florida’s coastal lifestyle, he had begun using his public profile for.
articles.body: Long before Jimmy Buffett became widely associated with island music, boats and Florida’s coastal lifestyle, he had begun using his public profile for a very different cause. Manatees were not always the familiar conservation symbol they are today. In the late 1970s and early 1980s, awareness of the animals and the dangers they faced was still growing, particularly as boat traffic increased across Florida’s waterways. Buffett became involved with the people trying to change that. What began with an early encounter with a manatee developed into years of campaigning, fundraising and public education, helping bring the animals into the view of a much larger audience.How Jimmy Buffett first became involved with manatee conservationBuffett’s interest in manatees grew from his connection with Florida and its waterways. His first encounter with one of the animals left a strong impression on him at a time when public awareness of manatee conservation was still limited.The animals faced threats that were closely tied to the way people used Florida’s rivers, springs and coastal waters. Fast-moving boats could seriously injure or kill manatees, while changes to their habitat created further problems. Conservationists were trying to persuade a much larger public that these slow-moving animals needed protection.Buffett was in a position to reach people who might never have encountered a conservation campaign otherwise. He was already a well-known performer, and his association with Florida gave the cause a natural connection to his audience.The 1981 campaign that put manatees in the spotlightIn 1981, Buffett became involved with Governor Bob Graham in establishing the Save the Manatee Committee. The organisation was created to increase public understanding of manatees and the dangers facing them in Florida.Buffett’s involvement went beyond appearing alongside politicians at public events. He took part in public service announcements and helped bring the subject into his concerts, where fundraising and awareness efforts could reach thousands of people at a time.A photograph from 1982 shows Buffett and aquatic biologist Patrick Rose reviewing a public service announcement script in Key West. Rose would remain closely associated with the campaign for decades.The partnership was unusual for a conservation movement. A professional musician had become one of its most recognisable public figures, while scientists and advocates supplied the expertise behind the message.How Buffett helped make Florida’s waterways saferBuffett used his concerts as a way to raise both money and attention for manatee protection. Funds were directed towards conservation work, including signs intended to warn boaters about manatees and encourage slower speeds in areas where the animals were present.The issue was relatively straightforward to explain. A manatee swimming near the surface could be difficult for a fast-moving boat operator to see in time, and collisions could cause severe injuries.Getting that message into everyday boating culture was harder.Public awareness campaigns helped make the animals more recognisable and gave people a reason to pay attention to speed restrictions and other measures designed to reduce collisions. Buffett's visibility gave those messages an audience far beyond the specialist conservation community.The idea that became Adopt-A-ManateeBuffett's involvement developed further in 1984, when he helped conceive the Adopt-A-Manatee program.The idea gave members of the public a direct way to support individual manatees while contributing to wider conservation work. It also turned an otherwise distant environmental issue into something people could engage with personally.Adoption programs were not new as a fundraising concept, but applying the approach to manatees helped build a connection between the public and animals that many people knew little about. Supporters could learn about particular manatees while their contributions helped fund conservation and educational activities.For the campaign, that combination of fundraising and public education proved useful. Manatees were no longer simply an obscure wildlife issue. They had become animals people could recognise, talk about and actively support.How Buffett connected manatee protection with Florida lifeThe campaign developed during a period when Florida was experiencing rapid growth and increasing recreational use of its waterways. Manatee protection therefore became closely linked with a much wider question about how people shared the state's waters with wildlife.Buffett's contribution was largely in communication and public reach. He did not replace the biologists, conservation groups or government officials doing the technical work. Instead, he helped carry their message into places they could not easily reach.His music also gave the subject a cultural connection. For audiences familiar with Buffett's songs about the sea, boats and Florida life, the manatee campaign fitted naturally into an existing relationship with the state's waterways. That association lasted for years.The quieter side of Buffett’s manatee advocacyBuffett remained involved with manatee conservation well after the committee was established. His support became part of the history of an organisation that continued working on public education, habitat protection and measures aimed at reducing human-related threats.Patrick Rose, who worked with Buffett from the campaign's early years, remembered the singer after his death in 2023 as someone who had been present from the beginning and had repeatedly offered his help when the organisation needed it.The photograph from Key West captures a relatively ordinary part of that relationship: Buffett sitting down with Rose to work through a public service announcement. It was not a concert or a major political event. It was campaign work.Those smaller contributions were part of how the cause reached the public.Manatees became a Florida symbol as conservation evolvedFlorida's manatees later became far more familiar to the public, and conservation efforts helped change their legal and management status over time. The species was once in a much more precarious position, with protection efforts focused heavily on preventing deaths from human activity.The population has since increased substantially from historic lows, although that recovery has not meant the end of conservation concerns. Boat strikes, habitat changes, water quality and other pressures continue to affect manatees. That makes the history of Buffett's involvement relevant beyond his own career. He entered the campaign when relatively few people were paying attention to the animals and helped make them part of Florida's broader environmental identity.For Buffett, manatee conservation became one of the less visible but enduring parts of a career that was usually defined by music. His role was not that of a scientist or wildlife manager. It was that of a prominent Floridian who used an existing audience to make an unfamiliar conservation issue harder to ignore.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Trump faces fresh setback as judge blocks stricter foreign student visa rule
articles.summary: US News: Another setback for President Donald Trump’s administration came on Monday after a federal judge blocked a new rule that would have imposed stricter l.
articles.body: Another setback for President Donald Trump’s administration came on Monday after a federal judge blocked a new rule that would have imposed stricter limits on how long foreign students and journalists can remain in the US.US District Judge F. Dennis Saylor in Boston issued the ruling a day before the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) was due to implement the policy. The rule would have ended the decades-old system under which many foreign students could remain in the country for the “duration of status” of their academic programme.Saylor ruled in favour of a coalition of unions and higher education advocacy groups that challenged the policy. He said DHS had adopted the rule based on “exceptionally weak” rationales, rejecting the agency’s arguments that the changes were necessary to combat visa fraud and strengthen national security.Judge warns of wider economic damageUnder the rule, F visas for international students and J visas for cultural exchange visitors would have been capped at four years. I visas for foreign journalists, which can currently remain valid for years, would have been limited to 240 days.Students would also have faced tighter restrictions on changing programmes or transferring between universities. The new system would have given them 30 days to leave the US after graduation or after changing to another visa category, down from the previous 60-day grace period.The Trump administration has argued that the changes are needed to prevent people from exploiting the student visa system by repeatedly enrolling in courses to remain in the US.DHS General Counsel James Percival criticised Monday's ruling, saying it would require US Immigration and Customs Enforcement to "permit this rampant abuse of our immigration system.""Come on a student visa, take one class per semester, and stay here for decades," he said.But Saylor, an appointee of Republican President George W. Bush, said the government had failed to properly consider the consequences of replacing a system that had operated for nearly five decades.He said the existing system had enabled tens of millions of foreign students and researchers to study in the US, contributing to "groundbreaking research in science, medicine, and technology, substantial economic growth, and a host of other benefits, often on a vast scale."The judge also warned that major research universities, including Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Harvard, could face hundreds of millions of dollars in costs and declining enrolment."The damage to the higher education system and to the economy of the United States is likely to be catastrophic," Saylor wrote.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Mystery missile in Yemen: Did Saudi Arabia use China-made DF-15A?
articles.summary: International News: Saudi Arabia may have launched a Chinese-made DF-15A ballistic missile in Yemen, after debris believed to be the missile’s booster was found in Marib .
articles.body: Saudi Arabia may have launched a Chinese-made DF-15A ballistic missile in Yemen, after debris believed to be the missile’s booster was found in Marib Governorate, according to visual imagery and open-source reports.The debris was reportedly found in Raghwan district of Marib, with images circulating online appearing to show a DF-15A designation on the missile component.The War Zone said open-source analysts had identified it as a DF-15A and attributed it to Saudi Arabia, but stressed that neither the missile identification nor its ownership has been confirmed.The reported discovery comes amid a renewed escalation in Yemen, where Houthi forces and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces are engaged in intensified fighting. The Houthis have also stepped up missile and drone attacks against Saudi targets, while Riyadh has increased strikes against Houthi positions.The DF-15A is a Chinese road-mobile, solid-fuelled short-range ballistic missile. According to the CSIS Missile Threat project, the DF-15 family has a launch weight of about 6,200 kg and can carry a 500-750 kg payload. Its range is estimated at 600-900 km, although the exact range varies by variant and payload.It uses an inertial guidance system and can carry a high-explosive warhead. Different DF-15 variants can also carry warheads designed to hit runways and hardened targets.Saudi Arabia has not officially acknowledged operating the DF-15A or any other short-range Chinese ballistic missile. However, previous reports have linked Riyadh to Chinese ballistic-missile systems, including the DF-3A, which Saudi Arabia publicly displayed in 2014, and the DF-21, whose reported sale to the kingdom has never been officially confirmed.The reported DF-15A debris therefore could provide a new indication of a previously undisclosed Saudi missile capability, if the identification and attribution are eventually confirmed.

articles.title: Bristol couples covered Pero’s Bridge with love locks, but 3 tonnes of metal eventually stopped the historic bridge from lifting
articles.summary: UK News: For years, couples visiting Bristol attached padlocks to Pero’s Bridge to symbolise their relationships, often throwing the keys into the harbour belo.
articles.body: For years, couples visiting Bristol attached padlocks to Pero’s Bridge to symbolise their relationships, often throwing the keys into the harbour below. The tradition eventually created an unexpected engineering problem. By June 2025, an estimated three tonnes of locks had accumulated on the pedestrian bridge, adding so much weight that it could no longer be lifted. The city planned to remove the locks before that summer’s Harbour Festival.How Pero’s Bridge became a symbol of romancePero’s Bridge crosses Bristol’s Floating Harbour, connecting Queen Square with Millennium Square. Opened in 1999, the pedestrian crossing was named after Pero Jones, an enslaved man who lived in Bristol during the 18th century. Its most distinctive feature is a pair of large horns that act as counterweights when the bridge is raised.Over the years, couples began attaching padlocks to the bridge as declarations of love, with the keys often being thrown into the water below. The collection became an instantly recognisable feature of the harbourside. Bristol24/7 reported in June 2025 that the locks had eventually accumulated to an estimated three tonnes.Three tonnes of locks stopped the bridge from liftingThe romantic tradition had gradually become an engineering issue. By 2025, the weight of the padlocks had become significant enough for a “no lift” notice to be placed on Pero’s Bridge, meaning it could no longer be raised because of the additional load.Patsy Mellor, Bristol’s director of management of place, told the city's harbour committee that the locks were estimated to weigh three tonnes. She said officials were looking for a solution that could allow the locks to be moved to a nearby structure instead. The removal had to take place before the Harbour Festival in July.The city had removed the locks beforeThis was not the first time Bristol had tried to deal with the growing collection. About a decade earlier, the council removed most of the padlocks from Pero’s Bridge, but people began attaching new ones and the bridge was covered again within a few years.The practice has also raised environmental and structural concerns elsewhere. Attaching metal locks can contribute to corrosion, while keys thrown into rivers and harbours can harm aquatic life. In 2023, a campaign was launched calling for the locks on Pero’s Bridge to be removed.The debate had previously gone in the opposite direction. In 2016, then Bristol mayor Marvin Rees said it was unlikely the locks would be removed, describing them as part of the creativity and iconic sights of the Floating Harbour.The love locks were due to be removedIn June 2025, officials said the three-tonne collection would be removed before the Bristol Harbour Festival, which was scheduled for July 18-20. Rather than simply throwing away the sentimental collection, the council was considering placing the locks on another nearby structure.The episode shows how a tradition intended to represent permanence can eventually clash with the infrastructure carrying it. Thousands of small gestures of affection had accumulated into a load measured in tonnes. The very symbols intended to keep love fixed in place had become heavy enough to prevent Pero’s Bridge from moving.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Meet Agimol Pradeep, Indian-origin UK nurse who won the Global Nursing Award worth $250,000 for increasing organ donation and transplantation within UK's South Asian community
articles.summary: UK News: Agimol Pradeep, an Indian-origin nurse based in the UK, recently won the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2026. On Saturday, Kerala Chief Minister.
articles.body: Agimol Pradeep, an Indian-origin nurse based in the UK, recently won the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2026. On Saturday, Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan presented the cash prize of $250,000 to the nurse at an event held in Kochi. It was Pradeep's contribution to greater awareness of organ and stem-cell donation over the years that gained her the recognition.A senior transplant coordinator at King's College Hospital and honorary senior lecturer at the University of Salford, she has emerged as the winner from more than 134,000 registrations from 214 countries and economies, from which 10 finalists were selected. The finalists were selected through a process involving Ernst & Young LLP, a screening jury, and a grand jury. They were assessed on their professional achievements, leadership, innovation, impact, and contribution to nursing. Nations including India, Sweden, Saudi Arabia, China, Colombia, Namibia, Nigeria and Papua New Guinea were represented through the finalists.“I have seen how a shortage of ethnically matched donors can leave patients from minority communities waiting for a life-saving transplant," she said, as per a report by The Week. She added that she considers the award as an opportunity to "take a lifetime of work further.""Half of the prize will support Upahaar and my mission to give more patients with organ failure and blood cancer a chance at life, by expanding organ and stem cell donation and taking this work to communities and countries where it is most needed," she explained.Upahaar is a charitable organisation aimed at increasing the awareness of organ donation among the South Asian community. Pradeep co-founded the organisation to identify the disproportionate impact of donor shortages on South Asian patients. The initiative has more than 10,000 stem cell donors registered.A scarcity of nursesSatheesan in his address highlighted the need to increase the nursing workforce. “The director-general of the World Health Organisation (WHO) has stated that there is a scarcity of 6 million nurses. We have also planned to increase the number of nurses in Kerala because healthcare is our priority.""I have seen how systemic barriers can prevent highly skilled nurses from returning to the profession," added Pradeep. She also said she wants to invest in nursing education and training to help empower more nurses to become changemakers.In a conversation with Gulf News, Pradeep highlighted the difference between healthcare systems that have established transplant services and those where such support remains limited. “In the UK, we have a dedicated organ transplant service where we have a national transplant waiting list. We can provide transparent care to patients who are struggling with organ failure.”But even in a developed healthcare system, the need has remained significant. “Despite saying that, we are losing around three patients every day with organ failure, even in a developed country like the UK.”"Stories of our top 10 finalists demonstrate that nurses are not only essential to delivering healthcare; they are shaping how healthcare evolves," said Aster DM Quality Care Ltd Executive Director Alisha Moopen. The award was first launched in 2021 and aims to bring together stories of nurses working across different healthcare settings, communities and disciplines, to signify the impact of nursing.Notably, the ceremony also featured a special message from Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, director-general of the World Health Organisation, who congratulated the finalists and recognised the contribution of nurses to healthcare worldwide.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Donald Trump called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang mid-interview and tells everyone he cannot take him on ...
articles.summary: Tech News News: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's appearance at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles took an unexpected turn when US President Donald Trump phoned in mid-conversa.
articles.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's appearance at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles took an unexpected turn when US President Donald Trump phoned in mid-conversation, using the moment to publicly dismiss growing concerns about AI posing an existential risk. According to a report by Business Insider, at the All-In Summit the interview of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was interrupted by a phone call from Trump. Speaking via speakerphone, Trump dismissed the fears of artificial intelligence as alarmist, declaring, “The robots will not be taking over.” He further added that while caution is necessary, the US should not halt AI advancement.Donald Trump positionTrump described AI doomerism as a “hoax,” reiterating his stance later on Truth Social: “Breaking another Hoax That AI is going to take over, consume, and destroy the World.” His remarks came amid growing debate in Silicon Valley over AI safety, following whistleblower Jacob Coxon’s resignation from Anthropic, where he warned that AI could “kill us all by the end of the decade.”A debate already roiling Silicon ValleyThe interruption landed in the middle of an already heated industry conversation about AI safety. The debate intensified after Jacob Coxon, a former Anthropic researcher, announced his resignation from the lab last week, writing on social media that people building the technology believe it could pose a threat to humanity's survival within the decade.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s responseDuring his talk, Huang struck a more measured tone than Trump's, praising Coxon for speaking out about AI safety while also pushing back on the broader idea that AI represents an existential threat, calling that particular framing unscientific. He said AI safety is paramount, while maintaining that the U.S. can continue moving quickly on AI development without sacrificing safety, arguing the country is capable of leading in AI while still doing so responsibly.Huang drew a clear distinction between Coxon's decision to speak up and the broader predictions being made about AI's future. He said he considers whistleblowing about problems inside a company to be legitimate, but views scientific-sounding predictions about the future as considerably less credible, since he argued they aren't actually grounded in science. He added that he doesn't personally know what Coxon witnessed while at Anthropic, and suggested that frontier AI labs more broadly are in the midst of a difficult transition from primarily research-driven organizations into engineering-focused ones.Get the latest technology news and updates.
